dataset.title: East Pacific Rise Field Record: a chemosynthetic vent interaction web

abstract.para: An attested, illustrative interaction dataset for the East Pacific Rise hydrothermal vent field (9-10 degrees N segment, north-east Pacific, at roughly 2,500 m depth). Occurrences — nine taxa including the focal giant tubeworm (Riftia pachyptila), its sulfur-oxidising bacterial endosymbiont (Candidatus Endoriftia persephone), and one human presence (Homo sapiens: deep-submergence research and prospective seabed mining) — are placed in the vent landscape and linked by resource relationships typed with OBO Relations Ontology terms. This is the Observatory's only trophic web whose primary production is chemosynthetic rather than photosynthetic: the base of the food web oxidises hydrogen sulfide from the vent fluid, with no sunlight in the chain. Taxonomy is the GBIF backbone (verified per-occurrence; the Candidatus endosymbiont is anchored to the accepted genus Endoriftia); interactions are sourced from the cited literature. Coordinates are representative of the East Pacific Rise 9 degrees 50 minutes N vent field (~9.83 N, 104.29 W). The vent field lies in areas beyond national jurisdiction, so no ISO 3166-1 country code applies. Ecological design produced under M19 Research Curator protocol (AI-OS v1.0). Design specification: .agents/decisions/2026-07-02-epr-dwca-design.md. Selection ruling: .agents/decisions/2026-06-27-third-cinematic-place-epr.md.
